commits.message:
Fix io_uring domain socket fd leak on multi-fd SCM_RIGHTS messages

Motivation:

CVE-2026-45536 hardened the epoll/kqueue native recvFd path
(netty_unix_socket_recvFd()) to reject truncated cmsgs, compute the
real number of fds from cmsg_len, and close any surplus fds. The
io_uring transport never received the same treatment:
IoUringDomainSocketChannel's IORING_OP_RECVMSG completion path
(CmsgHdr.readScmRights()) just read a single int at the cmsg data
offset with no check of cmsg_len, cmsg_level/cmsg_type or MSG_CTRUNC.

On 64-bit Linux CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(int)) and CMSG_SPACE(2 *
sizeof(int)) are both 24 bytes because of 8-byte alignment, so a peer
can pack two fds into a single SCM_RIGHTS message that fits entirely
inside the 24-byte buffer Netty sized for one fd. The kernel never
sets MSG_CTRUNC in that case, Netty only ever returns the first fd,
and the second is silently leaked. A peer of a channel using
DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS could repeat this to exhaust
the process's file descriptor limit.

Modifications:

- MsgHdr.getCmsgData() now reads msg_controllen (rejecting a
  completion with no ancillary data) and msg_flags (checking
  MSG_CTRUNC) from the completed msghdr.
- CmsgHdr.readScmRights() validates cmsg_level/cmsg_type, computes the
  actual number of delivered fds from cmsg_len via a new pure helper
  numFds(), and if anything other than exactly one well-formed fd was
  received, closes every fd that was actually delivered and throws an
  IOException instead of returning a partial (and leaking) result.
- Added Native.MSG_CTRUNC and Native.SIZEOF_INT JNI-backed constants
  and a Native.close(fd) binding, following the existing statically
  referenced constant/close-fd patterns, so the fix avoids hardcoding
  platform-specific values and doesn't need to allocate a
  FileDescriptor just to close a leaked fd.
- Added CmsgHdrTest, which exercises the numFds() arithmetic
  (including the exact 24-byte/2-fd scenario) as a pure function with
  no native library dependency.

Result:

io_uring domain socket channels in FILE_DESCRIPTORS mode no longer
leak file descriptors when a peer packs more than one fd into a
single SCM_RIGHTS control message.
commits.display_title: Fix io_uring domain socket fd leak on multi-fd SCM_RIGHTS messages

commits.message:
Validate SMTP command name for CRLF to prevent command injection

Motivation:

CVE-2025-59419 added CR/LF validation for SMTP request parameters but
left the command name unvalidated: neither SmtpCommand.valueOf nor the
SmtpCommand constructor nor SmtpRequestEncoder checks it. A command name
with embedded CR/LF (e.g. "NOOP\r\nMAIL FROM:<...>") therefore encodes
to several smuggled commands on the wire — the same injection class
(CWE-93) the parent CVE set out to close, on a field it did not cover.

Modification:

- Validate CR/LF in the private SmtpCommand(AsciiString) constructor,
the single construction path for all commands (cached constants and
valueOf alike).
- Widen SmtpUtils.validateSMTPParameter to package-private for reuse.
- Add a regression test asserting valueOf rejects CR/LF in the command
name.

Result:

A command name with CR/LF can no longer be constructed, so the encoder
cannot emit smuggled commands. This completes the CVE-2025-59419 fix
across both parameters and the command-name field.
commits.display_title: Validate SMTP command name for CRLF to prevent command injection

commits.message:
Validate chunked-must-be-last regardless of HTTP version (#17055)

### Motivation
RFC 9112 §6.1 requires that when a message uses Transfer-Encoding,
"chunked" must be the last encoding listed — a value like `chunked,
identity` is malformed. This rule was added to `HttpObjectDecoder`
alongside the fix for CVE-2026-42581, nested inside a pre-existing
`protocolVersion() == HttpVersion.HTTP_1_1` condition — the same
condition that gates a different, older check (the
Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding conflict handling).

Under the default configuration this is harmless: an earlier guard
already rejects any Transfer-Encoding header on a non-1.1 message
outright, so the ordering check's version scoping is not expected to be
exercised under normal use. However,
`HttpDecoderConfig#setUseRfc9112TransferEncoding(false)` is a documented
opt-out for restoring RFC 7230 behavior, and under that configuration a
non-1.1 message can legitimately carry Transfer-Encoding without being
rejected for it. In that case, the inherited version gate meant the
chunked-must-be-last check was silently skipped for HTTP/1.0 (and other
non-1.1 versions) — a message with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked,
identity` would decode successfully instead of being rejected.

### Modification

- Extracted the chunked-must-be-last check from inside the
`protocolVersion() == HTTP_1_1` block in `HttpObjectDecoder#readHeaders`
and gave it its own, version-independent condition, since the RFC 9112
ordering rule has no dependency on protocol version.

- Added two regression tests to `HttpRequestDecoderTest`: one
reproducing the original scenario (HTTP/1.0,
`useRfc9112TransferEncoding(false)`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked,
identity)`, and a companion using a non-no-op trailing encoding
(`chunked, gzip`) confirming the fix isn't tied to the specific encoding
that follows `chunked`.

- Corrected a pre-existing inaccuracy in
`handleTransferEncodingChunkedWithContentLength`'s javadoc, which stated
that earlier HTTP versions "will reject requests that include
[Transfer-Encoding]" without qualification — true only under the default
configuration, and already inaccurate before this change since
`useRfc9112TransferEncoding(false)` predates it.

### Result

- The chunked-must-be-last validation now applies to any message
carrying a Transfer-Encoding header, independent of protocol version or
the `useRfc9112TransferEncoding` setting.

Signed-off-by: husseinvr97 <husseinmustafabas05@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Chris Vest <christianvest_hansen@apple.com>
commits.display_title: Validate chunked-must-be-last regardless of HTTP version (#17055)
